ai.title: Fix unpaired tool calls for media-only outputs
ai.summary: Media-only tool results now emit an empty JSON tool message alongside the user image message to prevent unpaired tool call failures. Previously, `mediaToolResult` produced only a user message, leaving the assistant's tool call unanswered. The fix ensures tool messages always precede media messages in `common/src/util/messages.ts` to satisfy provider ordering constraints.

eli5.text: When the assistant asks for a screenshot or image-related tool, the response now always includes a brief text acknowledgment right before the actual image appears. This fixes a glitch where some image-only results were sent back without any matching reply to the assistant's request, which could make the conversation stop working. You wouldn't see the extra text, but conversations with image-returning tools now flow smoothly instead of occasionally breaking.

ai.title: Remove dedupeClientToolResults from agent runtime
ai.summary: Deleted `dedupeClientToolResults` utility and its invocation in `main-prompt.ts`. Client tool results now push directly to `messageHistory` without duplicate filtering. This reverts logic preventing provider errors on repeated `tool_call_id`s during SDK retries. Scope limited to `packages/agent-runtime`.

eli5.text: When you run something on the assistant's behalf, it used to quietly throw away any repeated command feedback before adding it to the ongoing record, to avoid confusing the AI provider. That duplicate-checking step has been removed, so repeated feedback now gets passed through directly. It only affects the internal agent runtime, and you wouldn't see anything change just by looking, unless you were watching how extra tool results get recorded after a retry.

ai.title: Base2 lite mode uses GPT-5.6-Luna and fixes BuffBench judges
ai.summary: Codebuff paid LITE mode now runs `openai/gpt-5.6-luna` via `LITE_MODEL` in `agents/constants.ts`, replacing previous DeepSeek usage. Freebuff free modes remain on MiniMax M3, with `code-reviewer-lite` restricted to wire compatibility only. BuffBench judging switched from a silent-failing 3-judge panel to explicit `judge-gpt` and `judge-sonnet` averaging, preventing single-model bias when Gemini judges 403.

eli5.text: If you pay for Codebuff's LITE mode, the assistant now uses a newer, faster, and cheaper model (GPT-5.6-Luna) instead of the previous DeepSeek model. You would notice responses may come quicker and cost less per interaction, though the overall experience stays the same. Free users are not affected. The way coding tasks are graded by the automated judge has also been made more reliable: instead of three judges where one could silently fail and skew the result, it now uses two specific judges and averages their scores, clearly warning you if one fails.

ai.title: Cloud planner pinned to MiniMax M3, build model split to DeepSeek V4
ai.summary: The Freebuff Cloud custom-stack planner now pins `CLOUD_PLANNER_MODEL_ID` to `FREEBUFF_MINIMAX_M3_MODEL_ID` instead of DeepSeek V4 Pro, while the post-plan build model is split into a new `CLOUD_BUILD_MODEL_ID` constant set to `FREEBUFF_DEEPSEEK_V4_PRO_MODEL_ID`. Three functions were added in `free-agents.ts` - `cloudBuildModelForAccessTier`, `isCloudBuildModelId`, and `resolveCloudBuildModel` - to select, validate, and coerce the build model per access tier and client request. A per-project turn ceiling `FREEBUFF_CLOUD_PLANNER_TURN_LIMIT` is set to `12` in `freebuff-models.ts` so a blank project cannot become an unbounded free premium-model conversation. The split ensures the build admits its own model-locked free session (avoids `session_model_mismatch`) because the build's token cost vastly outweighs planning. The `required_integrations` field on `cloud_plan_ready` now defaults to `[]` so a planner that cannot cite a Gravity `search_id` can still finalize instead of blocking the Start building button.
ai.evidence: In `common/src/constants/free-agents.ts`, `CLOUD_PLANNER_MODEL_ID` was reassigned from `FREEBUFF_DEEPSEEK_V4_PRO_MODEL_ID` to `FREEBUFF_MINIMAX_M3_MODEL_ID`, and `CLOUD_BUILD_MODEL_ID` was introduced as a new export pinned to `FREEBUFF_DEEPSEEK_V4_PRO_MODEL_ID`, with helpers `cloudBuildModelForAccessTier`, `isCloudBuildModelId`, and `resolveCloudBuildModel` added in the same file. In `common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts`, `FREEBUFF_CLOUD_PLANNER_TURN_LIMIT` is defined as `12`. In `common/src/tools/params/tool/cloud-plan-ready.ts`, the `required_integrations` field is now defaulted with `.default([])` and its description updated.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show the runtime consumer of `FREEBUFF_CLOUD_PLANNER_TURN_LIMIT` or confirm this constant is enforced yet, and it does not show which `runTriggerGates`/admission code calls the new `cloudBuildModelForAccessTier`/`resolveCloudBuildModel` functions. A second read of the same diff did not confirm that a migration step is required.

ai.title: Add log-scale TTFT histogram helpers for latency rollup
ai.summary: Adds `common/src/util/ttft-histogram.ts`, defining geometric bucket constants `TTFT_HISTOGRAM_BASE = 1.03` and `TTFT_HISTOGRAM_BUCKET_COUNT = 512` plus the functions `ttftBucketIndex`, `ttftBucketMs`, and `ttftPercentileFromHistogram` so hourly per-model TTFT samples can be summed into summable histograms for the /latency dashboard rather than stored as non-additive p50/p95 scalars. The new functions map a millisecond TTFT to a log-scale bucket index, recover the geometric midpoint latency for a bucket, and compute a nearest-rank percentile over unsorted `[bucketIndex, count]` pairs, returning null for an empty histogram. The module doc notes that `message_latency_bucket.bucket` is an index in this scheme and that changing BASE or BUCKET_COUNT silently reinterprets every existing stored row, so such a change means re-rolling the retained window.
ai.evidence: New file `common/src/util/ttft-histogram.ts` defines `TTFT_HISTOGRAM_BASE = 1.03`, `TTFT_HISTOGRAM_BUCKET_COUNT = 512`, and exports `ttftBucketIndex`, `ttftBucketMs`, `ttftPercentileFromHistogram`; its doc comment states `message_latency_bucket.bucket` is an index in this scheme and that changing BASE or BUCKET_COUNT silently reinterprets existing rows.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show a reader that actually writes `message_latency_bucket.bucket` rows or consumes these exports in a rollup, so the helper set is currently in place and does nothing at runtime.
